newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond fund net cash inflows hit record high.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond fund net cash inflows hit record high.

text.p: Net cash inflows of $760 million into U.S high-yield mutual funds for the latest week were the largest since AMG Data Services began tracking the data in 1992, according to AMG president Robert Adler.
Adler said the only other time weekly inflows exceeded $700 million was the last week of 1994.
The figures represent flows to high-yield mutual funds that report weekly, said Adler.
The numbers also exclude reinvested distributions, therefore representing only net new money coming into a fund, said Adler. This provides the most accurate measure of investor sentiment, he said.

Two Zurich Kemper high-yield funds received a combined total of $246 million in net cash inflows in the latest week. These inflows were the largest of all 230 high-yield funds tracked by AMG last week. They were also the largest inflows into all 2,772 taxable bond funds tracked by AMG, Adler said.

The Kemper funds had experienced some of the largest cash outflows during the recent correction in the high-yield market. The funds had net redemptions of $255 million in the week of April 2, according to AMG.

Analysts attributed such volatility to "market timers," a specialized type of money manager known for making large, short-term investments based on price momentum. The Kemper funds are known to be popular among market timer investors.
The recent surge in cash inflows could also be attributed to a positive fundamental outlook for the junk bond market, analysts added.
"People aren't particulary surprised (by the large inflows), because the economy is continuing to show record strength," said Walter McGuire, high-yield strategist at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
"High-yield investors are confident that the strength in the market still has some legs, even if we are at the peak of the business cycle," he said

According to AMG, a total of $1.32 billion in new cash has poured into high-yield mutual funds over the past three-week period. Junk bond funds experienced around $1.58 billion in net cash outflows in the four-week period prior to that, according to AMG.
